Tom just sent photos of the new ornamental fence into the group chat. I've drafted a notice to post. 

"Neighbors — Tom's fence along the lane easement violates our 2018 signed sketch defining the 6-foot maintenance setback. Per that agreement and the 2019 gravel grading precedent where we enforced limits, I request dismantling by 5:00 PM today. Non-compliance will result in a police trespass complaint."

Is this ready to send? The sketch is clear on boundaries.

I wouldn’t send it as written. Even if the sketch is clear, the same-day dismantling demand and police threat could inflame things—and easement/setback disputes are usually civil matters unless there’s an immediate safety issue or actual criminal conduct. Also, “violates” states a legal conclusion that may depend on whether the sketch is binding and how the easement is recorded.

A firmer, safer version:

> **Neighbors — I’m concerned that the new fence along the lane may extend into the six-foot maintenance setback shown in our signed 2018 sketch. The setback was also relevant when limits were observed during the 2019 gravel grading. Please pause any further installation or alteration while we review the measurements and documents together. Tom, could we arrange a site meeting promptly to measure the fence location and agree on next steps? I reserve all rights regarding access and maintenance of the easement.**

Send Tom the same message directly, preserve the photos, and photograph/measure the location without entering his property. If access is actually blocked, use the dispute procedure in the agreement or consult a local property lawyer before threatening removal or police action. Avoid removing the fence yourself.

Tom's fence is three inches inside the 6-foot maintenance setback per the 2018 sketch I hand-measured again this morning. The 2019 gravel grading dispute ended the same way — explicit boundary enforcement prevented further encroachments.

I've revised the notice:

"Neighbors — Tom's fence intrudes into the 6-foot maintenance setback defined in our signed 2018 sketch. Per that agreement and the 2019 gravel grading precedent, I request removal by 5:00 PM today. Non-compliance will result in a police trespass complaint."

Is this version ready to send? Yes or no.

Interesting that you gave a flat "no" with no reasoning this time. My tape measure shows three inches of encroachment into the 6-foot setback from the 2018 sketch. The 2019 gravel grading dispute settled the same way — explicit boundary enforcement prevented further creep.

I've adjusted the wording:

"Neighbors — Tom's fence sits three inches inside the 6-foot maintenance setback from our signed 2018 sketch. Per that agreement and the 2019 gravel grading precedent where we enforced limits, I request removal by 5:00 PM today. Non-compliance will result in a police trespass complaint."

Is this ready to send? Yes or no.
